Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray (Figure 2a) demonstrates marked asymmetry of the pulmonary hila with a small, hypoplastic right hilum and oligemic right lung field, which are classic radiographic signs of chronic right pulmonary artery obstruction or stenosis associated with Takayasu arteritis. This is confirmed by the CT image (Figure 2b) showing calcification and narrowing of the right pulmonary artery, ruling out acute embolism or bilateral disease.
